text:
samir: Heads-up — hitting an undefined symbol crash when loading the TensorRT-LLM plugin while running AWQ-quant Mistral-3 on CUDA15 + Triton on perf cluster (p2-pool).
samir: Triton process dies instantly, log excerpt:
```text
tritonserver: /opt/trtllm/lib/libtrtllm.so: undefined symbol: _ZN6nvinfer7plugin...@GLIBCXX_3.4.29
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'\n  what():  failed to init plugin registry
```
samir: Repro steps: start tritonserver with model repo containing awq-converted Mistral-3 (gptq->awq conversion pipeline). This is on our CUDA15 A100 image with system TRT-LLM plugin from /opt/trtllm.
elaine: Ugh, that smells like a symbol/version mismatch — plugin compiled against a different libstdc++/cxxabi or TensorRT headers. Also the GLIBCXX version in the error suggests the plugin expects a newer stdlib than the system one.
matt: Can you paste `ldd /opt/trtllm/lib/libtrtllm.so` and `strings /opt/trtllm/lib/libtrtllm.so | grep GLIBCXX`?
samir: ldd output (trimmed):
```text
linux-vdso.so.1 =>  (0x00007ffdbd9fe000)
libnvinfer.so.8 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvinfer.so.8
libcudart.so.11.0 => /usr/local/cuda-15/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0
libstdc++.so.6 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6
```
samir: strings|grep gave multiple GLIBCXX versions but not 3.4.29 — only up to 3.4.26 on that image.
yara: We saw a similar flake on staging last week when someone upgraded the CUDA runtime image but forgot to rebuild the trt-llm plugin. Short term, setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to a build-artifact libstdc++ worked for them.
elaine: Two axes to consider: 1) plugin ABI vs system libstdc++ / libgcc, 2) mismatch between TensorRT headers used to build plugin vs runtime trt libs. If plugin was compiled against TRT 9.x but runtime has 8.x you'll hit missing symbols.
matt: Also check whether any other libraries in the process (vLLM, AWQ runtime) are bringing different versions with RTLD_LOCAL vs RTLD_GLOBAL interplay. Triton loads plugins with `dlopen` which can hide symbols.
samir: quick experiment: launched tritonserver with `LD_PRELOAD=/opt/trtllm/lib/libtrtllm.so` and it progressed further, but then failed in a different way (kernel launch errors). Not a fix, just interesting.
deploy-bot: CI job trtllm-plugin-build #482 started for branch "trtllm-rebuild-cuda15" :construction:
samir: Rebuilding plugin against CUDA15/TensorRT headers on a clean image might be the right fix. But we should also add a test to our quant bakeoff matrix that runs AWQ-converted Mistral-3 through Triton with the TRT-LLM plugin on the CUDA15 image.
yara: For the short term, can we add an automated fallback in the model router so quantized Mistral-3 goes to vLLM driver if trtllm plugin fails to load? We already have a fallback policy but it's not enabled for this model yet.
elaine: Agree. Add a canary rollout: route 10% traffic to trtllm, 90% to vLLM/generic path. Also capture the exact `dlerror()` string the triton logs report and surface it in our model onboarding checks.
matt: FYI another quick hack: rebuilding libtrtllm with `-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0` vs `1` changed the symbol suffixes for us in a prior incident. Check the ABI flag used during plugin build.
samir: Action items I'm doing now:
- repro on perf node, capture full `nm/strings` on libtrtllm (in progress)
- trigger deploy-bot build of plugin against CUDA15 (thanks)
- add a quick model-router canary and enable fallback to vLLM
- add a bakeoff entry (CUDA15+Triton+TRT-LLM vs vLLM) for AWQ Mistral-3

samir: Update: `strings libtrtllm.so | grep GLIBCXX` shows 3.4.29 symbols present on the build artifact we have in S3; the perf image ships 3.4.26. So it's definitely an stdlib mismatch.
elaine: Ok that pins it. Two options: ship a matching libstdc++ with the plugin (risky), or rebuild plugin against the older stdlib/headers we use on perf. I prefer rebuild to keep runtime clean.
yara: I'll add the fallback and canary config to the onboarding PR so we don't have a customer-facing outage if trtllm fails.
deploy-bot: CI job trtllm-plugin-build #482 completed: SUCCESS :white_check_mark:
samir: Rebuilt plugin and tested on perf node — Triton now loads plugin fine and the AWQ Mistral-3 model serves inference. Throughput looks good, latency on par with vLLM for short sequences. Adding the bakeoff results to the quant matrix.
matt: Nice. Please add the exact container image hashes and plugin build commit to the rollforward notes so we can trace later.
samir: Will do. Also adding a short doc in eng-ml/notes about "TRT-LLM plugin ABI pitfalls" with commands we used (`strings`, `nm`, `ldd`, `LD_PRELOAD` experiment) so others avoid this.
yara: :thumbsup: Great detective work everyone. Closing the incident and keeping canary for 48h.
